items.title: Historical Factors and Emerging Developments
items.rights_note: IACCP's institutional history documents the Journal of Cross-Cultural Psychology's 1970 launch and the association's 1972 formation and Hong Kong congress; it is participant institutional history and not an independent history of every intellectual precursor.

items.title: The Influence of Culture on Visual Perception
items.rights_note: Open Library record for Segall, Campbell and Herskovits's 1966 comparative visual-perception study; only the catalogue record is cached, not the copyrighted book body, and its ecological hypotheses and sampled societies require historical rather than uncritical present-day interpretation.

items.title: Cross-Cultural Psychology: Research and Applications, Third Edition
items.rights_note: Open Library edition record and contents for a field-defining participant textbook covering cultural, comparative and indigenous traditions, methodology, theory and applications; the copyrighted book body is not cached or treated as read.

items.title: Culture + Behaviour + Comparison = Cross-Cultural Psychology
items.rights_note: IACCP conference repository record and abstract for Berry's participant programme: begin with ethnographic setting selection, link context to behaviour, then compare to test covariation and possible universals. It is a normative methodological position, not proof that all studies in the field follow it.
items.failure_note: The repository PDF endpoint returned HTTP 403 to a browser fetch; the publicly readable abstract record was selected without bypassing the restriction, and the paper body is not treated as read.

items.title: The Weirdest People in the World?
items.rights_note: UBC research-centre page reproduces the authors' abstract for a broad comparative review arguing that WEIRD samples are often unusual and insufficient for species-wide claims; the article body is not treated as read, and the argument does not make all between-population contrasts culturally causal or methodologically valid.
items.failure_note: The Harvard-hosted article PDF returned HTTP 403 to the collector; the UBC research-centre abstract record was selected without bypassing the restriction.

items.title: Decolonizing Psychology as a Scientific and Ethical Necessity
items.rights_note: Repository page and abstract, marked CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 on the page, critique universalizing WEIRD developmental models and exporting interventions without demonstrated local validity; the article body is not treated as read, and this is a forceful argued critique rather than a systematic review of every cross-cultural programme.

items.title: Many Labs 2: Investigating Variation in Replicability Across Samples and Settings
items.rights_note: LSE repository accepted manuscript reports preregistered replications of 28 findings across 125 samples, 15,305 participants and 36 countries or territories; exploratory WEIRDness contrasts and cross-setting heterogeneity concern these effects and samples, not universal cultural invariance.

items.title: The ITC Guidelines for Translating and Adapting Tests, Second Edition
items.rights_note: International Test Commission guideline sets preconditions, development, empirical confirmation, administration, scoring, interpretation and documentation requirements for adaptation across languages and cultures; following it supports but does not by itself prove construct equivalence, validity or fairness.

items.title: International Association for Cross-Cultural Psychology: About Us
items.rights_note: Current IACCP self-description documents continuing membership, congresses, publications and IUPsyS affiliation; institutional continuation does not validate every theory, national comparison or article associated with the field.
